method: Read-only verification of the 14 workbook rows: WebFetch on every workbook URL plus the two press-association aggregators (mddcpublicnotices.com, publicnoticevirginia.com) and the vendor/terms pages they pointed to; src/scrapfly_browser.py on the six pages that returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch (it confirmed HTTP 200 on four before the account throttled); WebSearch only to locate official pages (Fairfax CPAN, Spotsylvania Logan Systems, Free Lance-Star Column.us, MD Case Search's new host). No accounts created, no forms submitted, no Firecrawl, nothing under src/scripts run.

baltimore_county_md.notes: WebFetch got HTTP 403 (WAF); Scrapfly residential render returned HTTP 200 / 694 KB so the page is live, but the text could not be read back this session (stdout encoding crash, then Scrapfly throttled). Cadence sentence confirmed from the page's own search snippet. The docket is a next-day HEARING schedule, not a filings feed - new foreclosure complaints surface only via Case Search (CAPTCHA) or the mddcpublicnotices ad. MD is judicial: the first public signal is the Circuit Court foreclosure case (Case Search); the trustee's ad follows on mddcpublicnotices.com. Case Search is WAF-blocked to plain fetch (HTTP 403 on casesearch.courts.state.md.us, connection refused on portal.mdcourts.gov, Scrapfly empty) and the Judiciary's own Case Search FAQ (search-sourced) says CAPTCHA was added to confirm users are not robots or automated systems, so the court channel is CAPTCHA-gated with no bulk export; the ad channel is what the repo already scrapes.
